sections.risk_rationale: Guideline mandates strong normative claims (AI apps MUST have native multimodal support; text-only loses rich info) plus specific industry use cases/limitations backed only by general sources like YOvxh_ma5qE.

Strong claims on OCR cascade failures, rigidity, and non-scalability for agents (citing needed report numbers) transition to multimodal superiority, supported by OCR sources but with thin metrics on real-world fragility.
Descriptive theory on architectures/encoders/trade-offs follows Raschka figures and 2025 model lists closely; minor risk in superiority claims vs. OCR and diffusion comparison.

Guideline dictates verbatim step-by-step notebook walkthrough (specific functions like load_image_as_bytes, Pydantic object detection, attention_is_all_you_need.pdf, kitten/robot queries) as pre-scripted tutorial.
Presents ColPali as paradigm shift (2-10x faster, 81.3% nDCG) bypassing OCR, with specific architecture details from arxiv/HF sources that support but do not deeply validate all enterprise claims.

Heavily scripted explanation of notebook code with exact functions (create_vector_index, generate_image_description, specific queries like transformer architecture/kitten-robot), mocked multimodal embedding paths.
Prescribed step-by-step integration of search_multimodal tool into LangGraph ReAct agent with specific test question (kitten color) and system prompt; consolidates prior concepts descriptively.
Wrap-up connects to capstone project and Part 2 with mandated transitions; low risk as it stays high-level on using multimodal to avoid translation issues.

parsed.overall_notes: Implementation sections (S4/S6/S7) are predominantly pre-scripted tutorials with verbatim notebook steps and concrete examples (kitten PDF queries), pushing scripted fractions high while theory sections remain mostly evidence-seeking. Foundations are canonical (CLIP, VLMs, ColPali) with overlapping explanatory sources; dominant depth gaps in S1/S3 align with moderate argumentative risk on native-multimodal superiority claims.
